metadata.methods_description: Patients admitted for presurgical long-term video-EEG monitoring were simultaneously recorded with the Sensor Dot wearable device. One device recorded behind-the-ear EEG from electrodes on the mastoid, with placement depending on the suspected seizure onset. A second device on the chest recorded ECG and deltoid EMG. Each device sampled at 250 Hz and contained accelerometers and gyroscopes sampled at 25 Hz. Seizure annotations were formatted as BIDS-score compatible TSV files.

citation_details.title: Fusion-aware Ensemble Learning for Robust Multimodal Epileptic Seizure Detection Under Cross-dataset Distribution Shifts
citation_details.author: Abdul-Mumin Khalid, Musah Sulemana, Iddrisu Wahab Abdul
citation_details.venue: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
citation_details.abstract: Epileptic seizure detection using machine learning has promising results on benchmark datasets; reliable generalization to real-world clinical environments remains challenging due to inter-patient variability, sensor heterogeneity, and dataset shift.To address this limitation, this study proposes a fusion-aware decision-level ensemble learning framework for multimodal epileptic seizure detection using synchronized electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), electromyography (EMG), and accelerometer (ACC) signals.Twelve heterogeneous machine-learning and deep-learning models are trained on a unified multimodal dataset under strict patient-wise data partitioning to prevent data leakage.Classical ensemble strategies, including voting, bagging, boosting, and stacking, are systematically evaluated and compared with the proposed fusion-aware ensemble, which jointly optimizes multimodal fusion parameters and ensemble aggregation weights.We validated the proposed framework using multimodal data obtained from Tamale Teaching Hospital and the OpenNeuro public dataset.Following patient selection, the combined dataset was partitioned using a strict patient-wise 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% unseen testing protocol.The final 15% patient-wise hold-out subset was reserved exclusively for final evaluation to assess model generalization without patient overlap.Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieved 97.25% accuracy and 99.60% AUC on unseen data, and 95.25% accuracy with 99.00% AUC on the Patient-wise Unseen Test Dataset.These findings indicate that the proposed framework has strong potential for reliable multimodal seizure detection under realistic patient-wise unseen deployment scenarios and demonstrates strong discriminative capability on previously unseen patients.The results suggest that the proposed fusion-aware ensemble framework provides robust and reliable seizure detection under strict patient-wise evaluation.

citation_details.title: ECG-Based Detection of Epileptic Seizures in Real-World Wearable Settings: Insights from the SeizeIT2 Dataset
citation_details.author: Conrad Reintjes, Janosch Fabio Hagenbeck, Mohamed Ballo, Tim Rahlmeier, S.W. Wolf, Detlef Schoder
citation_details.abstract: Epilepsy is a prevalent neurological disorder where reliable seizure tracking is essential for patient care. Existing documentation often relies on self-reports, which are unreliable, creating a need for objective, wearable-based solutions. Prior work has shown that Electrocardiography (ECG)-based seizure detection is feasible but limited by small datasets. This study addresses this issue by evaluating Matrix Profile, MADRID, and TimeVQVAE-AD on SeizeIT2, the largest open wearable-ECG dataset with 11,640 recording hours and 886 annotated seizures. Using standardized preprocessing and clinically motivated windows, we benchmarked sensitivity, false-alarm rate (FAR), and a Harmonic Mean Score integrating both metrics. Across methods, TimeVQVAE-AD achieved the highest sensitivity, while MADRID produced the lowest FAR, illustrating the trade-off between detecting seizures and minimizing spurious alerts. Our findings show ECG anomaly detection on SeizeIT2 can reach clinically meaningful sensitivity while highlighting the sensitivity-false alarm trade-off. By releasing reproducible benchmarks and code, this work establishes the first open baseline and enables future research on personalization and clinical applicability.

citation_details.title: CMEpiNet: Complex-Valued Multimodal Epilepsy Detection Network Model
citation_details.author: Tianyi Su, Haiyan Zhu, Shuai Chen, Haifeng Wang
citation_details.abstract: Existing seizure detection methods cannot fully exploit the spatiotemporal features of multimodal signals. They also fail to capture deep associations among cross-modal features. This limits their ability to learn unified representations of spatiotemporal dependencies. This work proposes CMEpiNet (Complex-valued Multimodal Epilepsy detection Network model) to address this issue. CMEpiNet first uses complex-valued convolutions for feature extraction. It explicitly models phase synchronization, phase shifts, and cross-frequency coupling. Thus, EEG, ECG, and EMG features are represented in the complex-valued domain. During feature fusion, CMEpiNet uses a two-level semantic alignment-based fusion method. It applies cross-modal consistency constraints in a shared alignment space. It also performs distribution-level alignment in an epilepsy-related semantic latent space. These operations ensure the consistency of multimodal features in the global semantic structure. Finally, CMEpiNet uses a spatial attention-guided 3D convolutional classifier. The classifier jointly models the temporal, feature, and modality dimensions. Experimental results on the SeizeIT2 dataset show that CMEpiNet improves seizure detection sensitivity, reduces the false alarm rate, and maintains stable performance under perturbations.

citation_details.title: Privacy-preserving collaborative seizure detection from wearable EEG, ECG and EMG: analysis code and results for the SeizeIT2 validation
citation_details.author: Srinivasan Ramakrishnan, J. AROKIA RENJIT
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Analysis code and results for “Privacy-preserving collaborative seizure detection from wearable EEG, ECG and EMG: a large-scale validation on SeizeIT2” (Ramakrishnan S and Arokia Renjit J, 2026, submitted to Physiological Measurement). The archive contains the complete pipeline — quality control, feature extraction, per-recording normalisation, gradient-boosting and MLP baselines, simulated federated training (FedAvg, FedProx), differentially private training (DP-SGD via Opacus with Rényi accounting), membership-inference attacks with real non-members, and figure generation — together with every result table and figure in the paper. Data: SeizeIT2, OpenNeuro ds005873 (not included; download instructions in README.md). Licence: MIT.
